message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of several of the largest and most significant U.S. airports—by passenger traffic, hub status, or strategic importance:

| Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|
| **Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International** (ATL) | Atlanta, GA | ATL | Largest airport worldwide; key connecting hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| **Los Angeles International** (LAX) | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | Major gateway to Asia & Pacific Rim; busiest west coast airport. |
| **Chicago O’Hare International** (ORD) | Chicago, IL | ORD | One of the world’s oldest hubs; high domestic/International mix. |
| **Dallas/Fort Worth International** (DFW) | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | Large mid-size hub serving both domestic and international flights. |
| **Denver International** (DEN) | Denver, CO | DEN | Highest elevation commercial airport; growing hub for Southwest Airlines. |
| **John F. Kennedy International** (JFK) | New York City, NY | JFK | Primary East Coast gateway for transatlantic travel. |
| **San Francisco International** (SFO) | San Francisco, CA | SFO | Key West Coast hub especially for Asian routes. |
| **Seattle/Tacoma International** (SEA) | Seattle, WA | SEA | Important hub for Alaska Airlines and long-haul carriers like Emirates. |
| **Miami International** (MIA) | Miami, FL | MIA | Main entry point from Latin America and Caribbean. |
| **Orlando International** (ORF) | Orlando, FL | ORF | Heavy tourist traffic due to theme parks; busy seasonal operations. |

These airports serve as critical nodes for airlines such as American, Delta, United, Southwest, and many others, handling millions of passengers each year while supporting extensive cargo networks.
